ageing population = a situation in which the average age of people in a country is rising
birth rate = the number of live births per thousand people in a year
demographic change = a shift in the size or structure of a population
brain drain = the emigration of highly skilled people to other countries
wealth gap = the difference between the richest and the poorest in a society
underprivileged = not enjoying the standard of living or rights that most people have
marginalised = pushed to the edge of society and ignored by those in power
civil society = organisations and citizens acting independently of the state and the market
religious minority = a faith group that is smaller than the main religion in a country
interfaith = involving people of different religions working or talking together
civic engagement = citizens taking part in public life, from voting to volunteering
civil disobedience = deliberately breaking a law, peacefully, to protest against it
grass-roots movement = a campaign started by ordinary people, not by parties or companies
solidarity = unity and mutual support among people with a shared goal
social justice = the idea that society should be fair in how it shares rights and resources
positive discrimination = giving extra help to a disadvantaged group to make opportunities fairer
congregation = a group of people who regularly worship together
multiculturalism = the view that different cultures can live together and keep their identities
UN = the United Nations, an international organisation for peace and cooperation
EU = the European Union, a political and economic union of European states
